quiz.q: Which shortcut helps you find any action and shows its shortcut?
quiz.explain: Find Action searches every IntelliJ action by name and shows its key next to it.

quiz.q: You press Cmd+D on the line System.out.println("Squat"); and run. What happens?
quiz.explain: Cmd+D duplicates the line. Cmd+Backspace deletes it, Cmd+/ comments it.
Reformat only fixes indentation and spaces. The missing semicolon stays a compile error.
The middle line is a comment (Cmd+/), so Java skips it.

options: reached end of file while parsing
quiz.explain: The closing brace of main is commented out, so the class is never closed.

quiz.q: How do you open IntelliJ's terminal on a Mac?
quiz.explain: Option+F12 (Alt+F12 on Windows) opens the Terminal tool window in the project folder. Control+R runs the program.

quiz.q: Gym Log uses JDK 25. In IntelliJ's terminal on this Mac, java -version shows 23. Why?
options: The terminal uses the java on the PATH, not the project SDK
quiz.explain: The green triangle uses the project SDK (25); the terminal uses the system java on your PATH.

quiz.q: You run java Main.java with JDK 23 on a file with only void main() { IO.println("Hi"); }. What happens?
options: Error: implicitly declared classes are a preview feature
Error: cannot find symbol IO only
It asks which JDK to use
quiz.explain: Compact source files are a preview in Java 23 and final in Java 25. Use JDK 25 or --enable-preview on 23.

quiz.q: A Windows tutorial says Ctrl+D duplicates a line. What is it with the macOS keymap?
quiz.explain: In the macOS keymap most Ctrl shortcuts become Cmd, and Alt becomes Option.
